A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FacLens research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and material can be matched across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original prediction and runtime comparisons, cross-LLM transfer experiments, ablations, and a human evaluation involving 22 volunteers and 680 queries.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments, including the human evaluation in Appendix E, and adds HotpotQA results in Table 5.

M1.justification: The hidden-question representation, MLP encoder, classifier, cross-entropy training, MMD-based adaptation, dimension-matching projection and question-aligned minibatches remain unchanged. The HotpotQA evaluation introduces no method component.

E1.justification: v4 adds HotpotQA, extending evaluation to more complex multi-hop fact-seeking questions (Appendix D.4). PQ, EQ, NQ and the human-evaluation population remain, making this a limited extension of the existing factual-QA coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the retained experiments, including SAPLMA and INSIDE comparisons moved partly into the appendix. HotpotQA evaluates existing baselines; Entity-Popularity and SAT Probe are marked inapplicable rather than evaluated.

E3.justification: The retained experiments preserve the 20%/10%/70% split, greedy decoding, AUC metric, training settings and human-rating procedure. HotpotQA does not specify a distinct protocol or benchmark-specific sample counts and preprocessing; its addition does not establish a protocol revision.

E4.justification: The case study contracts from 12 successful examples and four failures to six successful examples and the same four failures. Removed examples include real-time knowledge questions. The layer/token comparisons, kernel analysis, transfer analyses and question-alignment ablation remain; relocated plots are not new analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Point-estimate and average-runtime reporting is unchanged, as are the human-evaluation counts and label-audit sampling information.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds HotpotQA results: middle-layer FacLens achieves 75.5, 66.9, 74.9 and 71.4 AUC% on LLaMA2, LLaMA3, Mistral and Qwen2, respectively. These are new benchmark results, not same-setting improvements. Tables 1–4, transfer heatmap values and human-evaluation totals are retained; six successful case entries are removed.

T1.justification: The binary NFP and transfer objectives, mixture-domain reasoning in Equations 2–4, and MMD/CE formulations remain equivalent. Splitting v2's PPL Equation 7 into v4's Equations 7–8 and explaining token notation adds exposition, not new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: v4 explicitly limits the title, abstract and concluding framing to fact-seeking QA, whereas v2 presents NFP more broadly. The central claims about question representations, efficiency and cross-LLM transferability remain.

C2.justification: v4 removes the response-interference explanation for SAPLMA comparisons, the middle-layer/Qwen mechanism discussion, and the demo screenshot's warning about unfamiliar topics. It adds an interpretation supporting applicability to complex questions through HotpotQA. The black-box and periodic-event limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-repository pointer and explains the existing LoRA rank/alpha choices, including their 1.95% trainable-parameter share for LLaMA2 (Appendix C.2). Most implementation details remain, but v2's explicit statement that SAPLMA uses middle-layer representations is omitted.

R1.justification: v4 adds Common Crawl, The Pile and The Stack citations supporting overlapping training corpora, plus HotpotQA. It removes KEEN and several representation-engineering and domain-adaptation references. Related work is regrouped into token-based and non-token-based approaches, while the transferable-NFP novelty position remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, method explanations and results discussion undergo extensive rewriting and compression. Human evaluation moves into Appendix E, experimental appendices are regrouped, and limitations move before the references. Fact-seeking terminology is applied throughout.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout. Figures 2, 3 and 5 are split between main-text PQ panels and appendix EQ/NQ panels; Figure 4 is rearranged and Figure 5 gains domain annotations. v4 adds Table 5 and removes the demo screenshot and six case boxes.

improvement.justification: The HotpotQA evaluation adds evidence for more complex questions, while clearer task framing and a code pointer improve scope and access information. These are modest gains: HotpotQA's setup remains underspecified, and some baseline details and research context are removed. The core method and established experimental evidence remain stable.
